That is the 0.5%-per-holder truncation floor, NOT a disclosure that nobody is short: any holder at 0.49% or below is invisible, and the baseline records this as anchor_covered: false / register_read_no_position. So there is no crowded short to squeeze and no building short to agree with, short_change_pct_pts is 0.0 by truncation rather than by measurement, and priced_lean_pct (+0.114) is essentially just -0.05 x run_up_20d_pct — i.e. the free control this stage has to beat. findings.why_not_priced: The FACT is fully priced — that is the finding. What is not priced is the event's own size: with two analysts and no option chain there is no implied move, and any ranker using the baseline's 5.27% proxy will size this print as if it could travel as far as a January trading update. If the market genuinely expected a 5% move into an audit confirmation you would see it in the tape — you would not see a stock sitting in a 167.5-177.0p band for a month on 60-120k shares a day. Instead the pre-print session printed 203,444 shares, still only ~GBP 350k of turnover, which is a thin de-risking, not an event being positioned for.

findings.finding: The one number that sets both the dividend and the P/E — adjusted EPS — is the number the market has NOT seen, and it is where the growth is leaking away: H1 FY26 adjusted EPS was exactly FLAT at 6.2p while gross profit rose 7.1% and adjusted EBITDA rose 6.4%, because adjusted PBT grew only 2.6% on rising amortisation of capitalised software (carrying value GBP 2.2m vs GBP 1.8m) and 'a modest rise in the effective corporation tax rate'. The 23 July update disclosed gross profit, adjusted EBITDA and TPV and gave no EPS figure at all.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time Fonix put a flat adjusted EPS in front of the market was the 17 March 2026 interims (6.2p vs 6.2p) and the stock moved +1.94% — i.e. it was looked through, because the interims also carried a +6.9% interim dividend and an upgraded international narrative. The comparable disappointment is 18 March 2025, -5.21%, the one interim where the delivery did not match the framing. So this line has been both looked through and punished within twelve months; the band is deliberately wide.

findings.why_not_priced: Adjusted EPS is the denominator of the dividend policy ('at least 75% of adjusted earnings per share') and of the 14.1x forward P/E the screens carry, and it is the only headline Fonix has never pre-announced. FY25 adjusted EPS was 11.3p (FY24 10.8p, +4.6%) and the house broker's FY26 number is 11.5p — +1.8% against adjusted EBITDA up 11.0%. If that gap were in the price you would not see a stock screened on a forward P/E and a 5.63% forecast yield with a 293p consensus target against a 171p close; you would see the target cut. With one house broker publishing (the company's own AIM Rule 26 page lists Cavendish as the only analyst), there is no second estimate to arbitrage the gap.

findings.finding: Fonix's ability to buy back stock is structurally capped by Rule 9 of the Takeover Code and almost nobody outside the RNS knows it: the concert party holds 33.05% of the share capital, so the company 'has historically been restricted in its ability to conduct share buyback programmes', and the GBP 2.0m 'buyback' every aggregator reported as completed was in fact a SINGLE purchase of exactly 1,250,000 shares (1.25% of capital) at a fixed 159p, only possible because Richard Thompson, through Starnevesse Limited, signed an irrevocable undertaking to sell alongside so the concert party's interest did not increase — his holding fell 7.362603% to 6.149129% in the matching TR-1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital return is the line that moves this stock most. The single largest observed reaction in the baseline's history is 2025-01-23, +5.83%, headlined 'Trading Update and Special Dividend Declaration' — the trading update alone a year later (2026-01-22, no special) moved +5.33%, and 2024-01-24 'Trading Update' moved +9.30%, so the specials are not the whole of it, but this is demonstrably a shareholder-return-owned register. FY26 broke the pattern: no special dividend was declared in January 2026 for the first time, and a GBP 2.0m structured buyback in May replaced it — on 22 May 2026 the shares closed at 159p, the buyback price, and did not re-rate.
findings.original_quote: Due to the Concert Party (as defined in the Company's admission document) in aggregate being interested in 33.05% of the Company's issued share capital (the 'Concert Party Percentage'), the Company has historically been restricted in its ability to conduct share buyback programmes to return value to shareholders given that any increase to the Concert Party's holding would require the Concert Party to make a mandatory cash offer for the entire issued and to be issued share capital of Fonix, pursuant to Rule 9 of the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers. However, Richard Thompson (through Starnevesse Limited, a company owned and controlled by Richard Thompson), a significant shareholder in the Company and a member of the Concert Party, has signed an irrevocable undertaking to sell up to 1,250,000 Ordinary Shares ... so as to ensure that on conclusion of the Share Buyback Programme, the Concert Party's aggregate interest in Ordinary Shares does not increase. [reconstructed from the PDF text layer via eu_pdftext.py]
findings.why_not_priced: The structure is only in the RNS PDF. TipRanks describes it as 'completed a GBP 2.0 million share buyback, reflecting strong cash generation and the board's confidence' (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/fonix-lifts-profits-and-steps-up-european-push-as-mobile-payments-pipeline-grows) and Kalkine as a 'GBP 2.0 million programme' — neither mentions Rule 9, the 33.05% concert party or the matching irrevocable, and the issuer's own 23 July summary of it says only 'the Group also completed a GBP 2.0m on-market share buyback, underlining the Board's confidence'. So the read available to anyone who did not open the May RNS is 'this company now runs buybacks', when the true read is 'this company can only run a buyback when a named 6.1% holder agrees to sell into it'. If the market knew, the finals' capital-return line would not carry an open-ended-buyback option in the price at all. The direction is modestly negative because it removes an upside scenario rather than creating a downside one: the promised increase in the FINAL DIVIDEND is the one return that needs nobody's permission, and it is contractually ~75-78% of an adjusted EPS that grew ~2% in H1.

Broadcast reports the Love Island 2026 summer series launched to 620,000 viewers on ITV2, its lowest ever for a regular summer series and roughly half the prior year (https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/digital-and-demographic-focus/love-island-2026-launches-modestly/5217604.article), and the bulk of that series sits in Fonix's Q1 FY27, which the finals' current-trading line covers. I drafted this as a -0.3 finding in the local pass and DROPPED it after reading LESSONS.md: Love Island's votes run through ITV's free app, Fonix's ITV revenue is the competition portfolio and SMS/interactive services across I'm a Celebrity, BGT, GMB and This Morning, and neither Fonix nor ITV has said the two are linked. Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and this one is not established.

UK carrier-billing regulation as a FY27 risk. Ofcom took over premium-rate services regulation from the Phone-paid Services Authority on 1 February 2025 and replaced Code 15 with the PRS Order (https://www.ofcom.org.uk/phones-and-broadband/mobile-phones/ofcom-takes-on-responsibility-for-regulating-premium-rate-services) — that is 19 months old, Fonix has traded through it, and I found nothing dated in 2026 that changes the economics before this print.

The FCA aggregated register is public only at 0.5% per holder, so anything smaller is structurally unobtainable; I did not spend a call on the per-holder history file because a name absent from the current aggregate has by construction no open position at or above the threshold to find.
